I fixed the core SEO issues on your Angular site so Google can actually crawl and render it correctly.

What I changed:
- Added a static canonical link and robots index/follow tag to src/index.html so they appear before JS runs.
- Added full Open Graph (og:title, og:description, og:url, og:type, og:site_name, og:image + dimensions) and Twitter card meta tags.
- Fixed SSR prerendering: updated src/app/app.routes.server.ts to list the real routes (/, /home, /funders, /projects, /investors, /founder-brief, /how-mrv-works, /terms-of-service, /privacy-policy) and fall back to server for 404s. Removed the invalid routesFile option from angular.json so the build passes.
- Set noindex and a 404 page title on the NotFoundComponent so accidental soft 404s don't leak into search results.
- Added structured data JSON-LD: Organization, WebSite, and BreadcrumbList in src/index.html.
- Added OG/Twitter image dimensions (1400x1400).

Build now passes and prerenders 9 static routes, which is exactly what Google needs.

content: we recently did the console implementation but i wanted to know the importance of sitemap

Here are the trade-offs of the current setup (no sitemap reference, but sitemap file still exists in the build):

**What you lose without a sitemap reference:**
- Google has to discover every page by crawling internal links. For a new or low-authority site, that takes longer, especially for pages that aren’t heavily linked.
- You lose the “Submitted vs indexed” report in Search Console, which is one of the best ways to diagnose indexing problems.
- If you add pages later, Google won’t know about them until it recrawls and follows a link to them.

**What you gain:**
- It’s one less thing to maintain. You don’t have to remember to update `robots.txt` if your URL structure changes.
- If your sitemap ever had bad URLs, Google wouldn’t be confused by it.

**Bottom line for your site:**
You have a small, well-linked site with only 9 routes, so Google will probably find all the pages either way. The sitemap won’t make or break your rankings. But it does speed up initial indexing and gives you better diagnostics in Search Console, which is valuable right now while the site is new.

So it’s not urgent, but it’s still a slight net positive to reference it.
